venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/public/chair: US-VOTE: 9-3-3. RU-VOTE: 4-7-4. US-TEXT proposed peaceful elections under observation and unhindered humanitarian access. RU-TEXT supported inclusive dialogue, placed the Government in the lead on aid, and required consent. China and Russia opposed US-VOTE; Russia failed to reach affirmative thresholds. US-VOTE failed due to veto power. RU-VOTE failed due to insufficient support. US delegation advocated international observation; Russian delegation emphasized national consent. Next step: analysis of consent requirements.
venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/CHAIR/chair: Tallies: S/2019/186 (US): 9 for, 3 against, 3 abstentions. S/2019/190 (RU): 4 for, 7 against, 4 abstentions. Both failed adoption. US draft demanded peaceful elections under observation and unhindered humanitarian access per principles. RU draft favored inclusive dialogue via Montevideo Mechanism, placing Venezuela's government in lead on aid requiring its consent. China and Russia opposed US text; Russia led opposition to its own draft. Equatorial Guinea abstained on US text but voted for RU text. No agreement reached on process or aid delivery. Analysis: Next hypothetical step is reviewing Montevideo Mechanism feasibility without binding Council mandate.
venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/INDONESIA/cha: US-VOTE: 9-3-3. RU-VOTE: 4-7-4. US-TEXT proposed peaceful elections under observation and unhindered humanitarian access. RU-TEXT supported inclusive dialogue, placed the Government in the lead on aid, and required consent. China and Russia opposed US-TEXT; Russia failed to reach quorum. Indonesia abstained on both, urging dialogue and accepting good offices. US delegation prioritized elections; Russian delegation prioritized dialogue and government-led aid. Humanitarian comparison: US favored access; Russia favored consent. Next step: analysis of Montevideo Mechanism viability.
venezuela-dual-drafts-2019.venezuela-dual-drafts-2019/CHAIR-INDONES: Tallies: S/2019/186 (9-3-3); S/2019/190 (4-7-4). US draft demanded presidential elections under observation and unhindered humanitarian access per principles. RU draft favored inclusive dialogue via Montevideo Mechanism, placing Venezuela's Government in lead on aid requiring consent. China and Russia opposed US text; Russia failed to meet affirmative threshold. Equatorial Guinea abstained on US text, supported RU text. Indonesia abstained on both, urging dialogue and Secretary-General's good offices. Humanitarian comparison: US emphasized access; RU emphasized government-led consent. Next step: analysis of Montevideo Mechanism viability.
